topics.topic: Credential scan inputs, protected-value set, byte boundaries, and exact verbatim-match semantics
questions: What exact representation and comparison define a verbatim credential match in arbitrary answer bytes?
Which protected values are searched for, and at what point are they snapshotted when configuration or credentials can change during a request?
Which protected values are credentials for this search, and what constitutes a verbatim match, including byte encoding, case, delimiters, empty values and rotated or inactive credentials?

What bytes are searched: the raw HTTP entity, content-decoded bytes, a parsed structured body, individual multipart parts, streamed chunks including cross-chunk matches, error bodies, and partial bodies from interrupted responses?

Which bodies, credentials and byte representation does the kernel search: only the credential used for that service call or every configured secret, and before or after transport decoding, parsing and file extraction?

What exact transformations count as “another encoding” rather than verbatim—for example JSON escaping, multipart framing, HTTP content encoding, character encoding, or a credential embedded as an exact byte substring in a larger binary file?

quotes: resolve_service_credential: [BEHAVIOR] MUST find the service_credentials entry of service_id and read, at this call and never earlier, the file at its secret_file path, opened component by component without following a symbolic link at any component, the checks and the read using that one opened file, which must be a regular file, owned by the process's effective user and granting no permission to group or others; the value is the file's content decoded as UTF-8 with exactly one trailing newline removed when present.
resolve_service_credential: [RETURN_SHAPE] Returns ResolvedCredential with the configured header_name and the resolved header_value, for the one request being built.

The kernel asks for no content encoding (`Accept-Encoding: identity`); the
   size counted is the response body's bytes after transfer decoding.

Every body as read, whatever its status — reading stops at the ceiling
   (rule 5) — is searched, before it is parsed or cut, for the bytes of the credential
   value sent with the request; when they occur, the body is
   dropped whole and `failure_detail` is exactly `error body withheld: it
   contained the credential` (A17 rule 2).

Only that verbatim echo is
   searched for; a body carrying the credential in another encoding is kept
   like any other and is protected only by its class.
judgement.why: The later service and installation rules define the search as an exact byte-subsequence match against the credential resolved for and sent with that request, over transfer-decoded response bytes before parsing or extraction.

topics.topic: Observable result and withholding scope when a credential match is detected
questions: What observable node and run result replaces an answer when a verbatim credential is found?
If one part or included file matches, is the entire operation answer withheld or only the affected file or output port?
When a match is detected, what observable node and run status, refusal or failure reason, trace record, and caller-visible result are produced?

What observable node and run result occurs when the search finds a credential, including whether the entire operation response or only the matching file/value is discarded and which failure reason is recorded?

judgement.why: This asks the same observable node, run, withholding and downstream-result question already decided by P2, and the cited later passages have not changed.

precedent.topic: Node and run outcome after detecting an echoed credential
quotes:
A 2xx body that echoes it is
   therefore not used: the answer is `contract_violation` (rule 5), no output
   is stored or spooled, and for a non-read operation the attempt is `applied`
   (owner, 2026-10-05: a stored output holding the credential would be the
   kernel writing it).

A failed node stops only its dependants (`upstream_failed`); independent
branches finish (K-09).
precedent.why: The later rules make the node a contract violation with the fixed withholding detail, store no output, mark a non-read attempt applied, and stop only dependent nodes.

topics.topic: Storage, retention, and verified disposal of matched credential-containing bytes
questions: May bytes containing the credential ever enter the run spool, and if they do, must they be deleted immediately rather than retained with a failed run?

Is a matched body or file discarded immediately, or may it remain in the run spool, failed-run retention, trial evidence, temporary storage or backups; and what stored fact proves its disposal without recording the credential?

May a matching body or file be written to the run spool or other kernel storage while it is scanned, and must it be deleted immediately so that a failed-run capture cannot preserve it as a trial fixture or later pass it to a function?

judgement.why: This asks the same storage, spooling, retention and disposal question already decided by P5, and the cited later passages have not changed.

precedent.topic: Retention or deletion of credential-bearing bodies and derived records
quotes:
when they occur, the body is
   dropped whole and `failure_detail` is exactly `error body withheld: it
   contained the credential` (A17 rule 2). A 2xx body that echoes it is
   therefore not used: the answer is `contract_violation` (rule 5), no output
   is stored or spooled, and for a non-read operation the attempt is `applied`
   (owner, 2026-10-05: a stored output holding the credential would be the
   kernel writing it).

A 401 whose body echoes the credential value keeps `failure_detail` exactly
   `error body withheld: it contained the credential`, and the credential
   appears in no record.

A 2xx JSON body that echoes the credential value in a member an output port
   takes concludes `contract_violation` with that same `failure_detail`, and
   no StoredValue holds the credential.
precedent.why: The body is dropped whole, never stored or spooled as output, and the credential appears in no record or StoredValue, leaving only the fixed non-secret failure detail.

topics.topic: Scan limits and handling of answers that cannot be completely searched
questions: What happens when the kernel cannot complete the credential search, for example because the answer exceeds a bound or its stream terminates with an error?
What size, time and streaming limits govern the search, and what happens if the body cannot be completely searched because it is too large, malformed, interrupted or unreadable?

judgement.why: This asks the same bounded-search and incomplete-response handling question already decided by P1, and the cited later passages have not changed.

precedent.topic: Behavior when credential scanning cannot be completed
quotes: send_prepared_request: [BEHAVIOR] MUST bound connecting, writing and reading the whole response by one deadline, the monotonic_ns reading taken before connecting plus the imported RELEASE_CEILING_TRANSPORT_TIMEOUT_MS constant in nanoseconds, held in a local variable only and never stored; each socket wait is given the time left rounded up to whole milliseconds, and the deadline has passed once a later monotonic_ns reading reaches it; the response body is counted after transfer decoding and read at most to the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SERVICE_RESPONSE_BYTES_MAX constant, a longer body being over the ceiling.

send_prepared_request: [BEHAVIOR] The outcome is decided in this order, with effect_class read meaning the read column: a failure of name resolution, connection or TLS before the first request byte was written is service_unreachable, attempt not_sent for other classes; a timeout, reset, end of stream, malformed status line or headers — a status line and header section longer together than the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SERVICE_RESPONSE_BYTES_MAX constant included —, or only 1xx after the first byte was written is service_unreachable for read and outcome_unknown with attempt unknown otherwise; 3xx is operation_failed with detail redirect_not_followed for read and outcome_unknown with attempt unknown otherwise; 5xx is service_unreachable for read and outcome_unknown with attempt unknown otherwise; 4xx is operation_refused, attempt not_applied for other classes; 2xx whose body is longer than the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SERVICE_RESPONSE_BYTES_MAX constant, whatever its output ports, or whose body as read contains the bytes of the credential value sent, searched before parsing, or whose outputs do not fit is contract_violation, attempt applied for other classes; 2xx whose outputs fit is succeeded, attempt applied for other classes.
precedent.why: State 8 notes define bounded post-transfer reading and classify read failures, timeouts, premature ends, oversized bodies and searchable bounded bodies.

topics.topic: Effect status and retry policy when a credential-bearing response is withheld
questions: If a state-transition, external-effect or destructive request was accepted by the service but its response is withheld for a credential match, is the effect recorded as applied, failed, or outcome_unknown, and may it ever be resent?
